subject: RTBF & backups: confirmation of scope, timeline, and evidence

Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RTBF & backups: confirmation of scope, timeline, and evidence

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what we'll deliver from Redwood to support FinApps' RTBF/compliance needs. Please confirm or correct any items below.

Key points we captured on the call
- PII types in scope: user names, email addresses, payment instrument last4, device IDs, and free-text notes (customer support transcripts).
- Retention: application tier currently keeps 365 days; backups (EBS snapshots + S3 archival) have a 30-day snapshot retention and 1-year archival lifecycle for cold storage.
- Residency: production is in us-west-2; FinApps requires EU residency for a subset of EU customers — outside scope of this ticket but flagged.
- Delete/RTBF expectation: FinApps wants evidence of irreversible deletion within 72 hours for active store data; understands backups may have constraints.
- Evidence: FinApps needs a signed statement plus machine-readable audit (deletion events + timestamps + auditing handles) and optional KMS key rotation confirmation if relevant.

What Redwood proposes (next steps)
1) Qualification: we will identify which datasets are primary vs. cached/backup and mark the requestable identifiers. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Deletion runbook: deliver a playbook that shows primary data purge + snapshot overwrite options and expected timelines. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Evidence package: provide audit logs (S3 object-level, KV cache purge events) + a written attestation and a timeline for backups. Note: for AWS snapshots we can show snapshot deletion events and the account audit logs; immediate irreversible purge of snapshot content is constrained by cloud provider snapshot semantics. (Owner: Redwood Compliance)
4) Contract/ops: if FinApps requires SLA for backup purge <30 days, Redwood will scope an exception path (reserved capacity + contractual acceptance of potential snapshot forensics). This will require an addendum to the contract. (Owner: Sales/Legal)

Attachments: Redwood-RTBF-proposal-v1.pdf (high level playbook & timeline)

Immediate asks for FinApps
- Confirm the list of PII elements above and specify whether transcripts are in scope.
- Which customer identifiers should be considered global vs. EU-only (if any)?

Proposed timeline
- Qualification & mapping: 3 business days after confirmation
- Draft deletion runbook: 5 business days after mapping
- Evidence package sample: 7 business days after runbook signoff

If that looks good I'll start the mapping and loop Marissa in for the technical runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the thorough recap. Couple clarifications from our side:

1) Transcripts: yes, support transcripts are in scope — they contain email addresses and sometimes SSNs that our agents redacted manually.
2) Backups: our infra team confirmed snapshots are AWS EBS snapshots retained 30 days, and we have an additional archival lifecycle that moves older data to Glacier for up to 1 year. From our compliance perspective we need the following from Redwood:
   - Confirmation whether Redwood can purge data from application-level stores immediately and provide a timestamped audit of deletion.
   - Outline what evidence Redwood can provide for snapshot-level deletion; we understand snapshots are immutable objects but need a clear policy on how those are handled and what evidence is available.

We want to be clear: for active customer deletion requests we expect primary store deletion within 72 hours. For backups we accept that provider semantics may extend the effective purge window, but we need a written description of that window and the evidentiary artifacts Redwood will provide. If possible, show example log lines or a sample audit.

Assignee for FinApps: Aisha (privacy@finapps.com) — she'll own signoff on the evidence package.

Once we have your runbook + sample evidence we'll review internally and confirm whether we need an SLA addendum.

Best,
Samir Rao
VP Product, FinApps

Hi Samir — looping in the technical details from our ops/runbook side. Quick answers and an extract from the runbook: see attached diagram (snapshot-deletion-flow.png).

Short answers
- Application-level stores: Redwood will delete records from primary DBs (Postgres/Bigtable-style) and from our object store indexes immediately once the request is processed. We record object deletion events into our audit stream (immutable append-only log) and can export a signed, timestamped CSV with affected ids and deletion tokens.
- KV caches & inference artifacts: ephemeral caches (in-memory/redis) are cleared immediately. Persistent inference artifacts (model metadata, cached responses saved to S3) are removed on deletion; S3 delete markers are applied and documented.
- Backups & snapshots: EBS snapshots are immutable. Our standard process is: mark snapshot for deletion -> issue DeleteSnapshot API call -> cloud provider runs internal GC. We can record the DeleteSnapshot call and the provider-side event id, but the snapshot blob may still be restorable by provider for a short window (provider-specific). For Glacier/cold archives, deletion follows provider lifecycle rules.

Evidence we can provide
- Signed CSV of deletion events with UTC timestamps and request id.
- Audit log export (CloudTrail-like events) showing DeleteObject/DeleteSnapshot API calls and associated request IDs.
- KMS key-wrap evidence showing the key rotation or key destruction event if FinApps requires cryptographic isolation. Note: actual key destruction is irreversible and requires legal acceptance.

Exceptions & timeline constraints
- Immediate irreversible deletion from backups is not always possible due to provider retention; typical snapshot GC is within 24–72 hours after DeleteSnapshot but varies and cannot be guaranteed sub-24 for all cloud providers.
- If FinApps requires contractual guarantee for <30-day backup purges, we'll need an SLA addendum and a scoped operational runbook (we can propose a premium remediation path).

Next steps (technical)
- I'll produce a sample evidence bundle (CSV + sample audit lines) within 3 business days.
- If you need cryptographic attestation, we can outline KMS handling and estimated lead time (5–10 business days).

Attachment: snapshot-deletion-flow.png (diagram of deletion + snapshot lifecycle)
